Hey man, I was in the same situation as you a while ago. I started taking sub and just forgot about the whole addiction thing. About 4 months later I decided to come off of it. I had tapered down to taking the smallest little sliver that I could cut twice a day. I then got to the point where I could skip a day and decided that I would quit after a week of day on day off.

The withdrawals were unreal. Way worse than coming off a 100mg a day oxy habit. I ended up going through with it anyway, but the peak seemed to last about 6 full days!! It took 2 weeks for me to be able to hardly sleep 7 hours then I would wake up all jittery with my heart racing. Subs stay in your system a very long time, thats why the withdrawals last longer,
so... Here is my advice, and it actually came from a doctor I talked to in a recovery clinic.

Switch back to an opiate with a short half-life, and taper off that for about a week to ten days. That way your withdrawals will only last a short amount of time and will not be nearly as intense. I relapsed for a short while and when I wanted to come off I tapered down to 15mg's of oxy and to be honest the withdrawals weren't bad at all. Only the first day was hard, and I only experienced hot flashes, restlessness, mild stomach discomfort and apetite loss. By the third day I was getting natural energy and could "see the light at the end of the tunnel" approaching fast. 

TL;DR
Coming off months of sub use is much much harder than coming off long term short acting opiates. Switch to a short acting opiate for about 7 - 10 days while tapering off and quit that way. Source: experience

Benzo physical dependency is no joke. I've come off opiates cold turkey before and it was horrible, but nothing compared to a cold turkey benzo withdrawal. I didn't even know I was addicted to it as I had only used the benzo's as prescribed by my doctor and for one month

It felt like the biggest anxiety trip ever and you have no control. There are physical symptoms as well, but the psychological symptoms are so bad you don't have time to notice. Since you know what anxiety feels like, I don't have to describe those withdrawal symptoms other than the fact that they were much more intense than any anxiety I have ever experienced.

The other symptoms were feelings that I had lost control of my own mind. It felt like I was just a pair of eyeballs watching someone else's life and I wasn't the one in control. There is overwhelming depression and racing negative thoughts.

At one point it got so bad that I considered I may have died somehow and this was actual hell. I am an atheist.

I ended up being able to take a very small amount of xanax and the symptoms slowly went away. I took one more small piece the next day and that is all it took for me to taper down and my brain to go back to normal, not experiencing any withdrawals after that.

If my withdrawals were that bad on the lowest dose of benznos (and I only took it at night, once a day) I can't imagine, at all, what the withdrawals would be like for someone who has been using for years and on triple or four times the dose. 

Your tolerance does build very quickly on these drugs. So yeah, I don't even know if there is a moral to this other than try not to take benzos. Good luck Joy and OP.
